bdl-ca-state.tell: A single US state reaching past its border through revenue and volume thresholds — the strongest evidence that the US answer to privacy is a patchwork, not an omnibus law.

bdl-can.tell: The commercial-activity statute where accountability is sticky: outsourcing the processing never outsources the responsibility, wherever the processor sits.

bdl-cn.tell: GDPR-shaped on consent and rights, but its transfer chapter points inward — the state gates the exit, which is localization pressure rather than an adequacy bridge.

bdl-coe.tell: A treaty about prosecutions rather than privacy — it moves offences and evidence across borders by obligating governments to cooperate, and never binds a company directly.

bdl-dpf.tell: The corridor that keeps dying in court — Safe Harbor fell, Privacy Shield fell to Schrems II, and this framework is the current adequacy bridge holding EU-to-US flows open.

bdl-eu.tell: The regime that exports its own rulebook: lawful transfer runs through an adequacy finding or contract-grade safeguards, and the obligation follows the person the data describes, not the server it sits on.

bdl-map-transfers.prompt: Match each instrument to the regime that enforces it — then read what it really does to data crossing that border.
bdl-map-transfers.note: Markers sit at the real coordinates of each regime's seat or geographic center, projected onto a Miller-style world map; labels in dense regions are nudged clear of their marker. Instruments, transfer rules and effective dates are authored from Chapple CISSP SG 10ed ch.4 and the Moore Domain 1 objective notes.
bdl-map-transfers.legend[0].label: Omnibus privacy law with transfer restrictions
bdl-map-transfers.legend[1].label: Sector-by-sector or state-level rules
bdl-map-transfers.legend[2].label: Voluntary principles or export-control arrangement
bdl-map-transfers.legend[3].label: Adequacy corridor or multilateral agreement
bdl-map-transfers.projection.note: x/y are derived at build time from lat/lon by the knowledge module's prepare() step; the board renders on the shared tools/templates/world-map-paths.svg asset that build_lab.py inlines for any lab with an aigpMap game.

bdl-oecd.tell: Principles, not penalties: the eight-point vocabulary most national privacy laws later borrowed, paired with an explicit plea to keep data moving across borders.

bdl-us.tell: A patchwork keyed to industry rather than to the individual — and its law-enforcement reach statute follows the provider across borders, which is the opposite direction from a data-localization rule.

bdl-wassenaar.tell: Not a privacy instrument at all: it controls what crosses the border when the export is the technology — and only as strongly as each member writes it into national law.

bdl-za.tell: Eight enumerated conditions and a dedicated regulator — its border test asks whether the destination's law looks like its own, a similar-protection rule rather than a contract mechanism.
